entries.clue: Doctor pried into case of somebody regarding some handwriting? (7)

indicatorNotes.Doctor: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters get rearranged
indicatorNotes.into: the rearranged letters go into the case
indicatorNotes.case of: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A nosy doctor has been rummaging through someone's file and is commenting on their scrawl.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: spidery describes thin, straggling handwriting rather than meaning 'regarding' it.
annotation.definitionFit: Spidery writing has long thin strokes like a spider's legs.

entries.clue: Individual inspired by seaside feature is trailblazing kind (7)

indicatorNotes.inspired by: to be inspired is to be breathed in, so ONE is taken inside PIER

blocks.note: a pier juts out to sea at a British resort

annotation.surface: Someone takes their inspiration from the seaside and turns out to be adventurous.
annotation.walkthrough: "Inspired" reads as motivated; its literal sense, breathed in, is the one that works the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A pioneer is someone who blazes a trail for others.

entries.clue: Daughter beginning to imbibe drink gets to start eating (3,2)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of imbibe is its first letter

annotation.surface: A daughter has a drink before tucking in to a meal.
annotation.walkthrough: "Gets to" is only a link; the definition is the phrase after it.
annotation.definitionFit: To dig in is informally to begin eating heartily.

entries.clue: Criticism found on left for link (7)

indicatorNotes.found on: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship

annotation.surface: Criticism from the political left is levelled at some connection.
annotation.walkthrough: "Left" looks political, but sailors call the left side of a ship port.
annotation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close connection or bond between people.

entries.clue: Corps deployed around two points in series of steps (7)

indicatorNotes.deployed: troops deployed are spread out and rearranged
indicatorNotes.around: the rearranged letters go around the two points

annotation.surface: An army unit is sent out to take two positions in a set sequence of manoeuvres.
annotation.walkthrough: The points are compass points, not places or positions.
annotation.definitionFit: A process is a series of steps taken to reach an end.

entries.clue: By the sound of it, given a direction and fixed in a firm way (6)

indicatorNotes.By the sound of it: tells you to go by what a word sounds like

blocks.note: given a direction means sent along a route

annotation.surface: Someone told which way to go ends up firmly stuck in place.
annotation.walkthrough: In British English route rhymes with root, so routed and rooted sound alike.
annotation.definitionFit: Something rooted is firmly fixed, like a plant in soil.

entries.clue: Small sausage from joint varying a lot in California (9)

indicatorNotes.varying: the letters of a lot vary their order
indicatorNotes.in: being in a state means sitting within its borders, so the pieces sit within CA

annotation.surface: A cut of meat in California yields sausages of all sorts of sizes.
annotation.walkthrough: A chipolata is a thin British sausage, often served wrapped in bacon.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the name comes via French from Italian cipollata, a dish flavoured with onion, and it now means the thin cocktail-size banger.

entries.clue: Distinctive exercise with agents put in confines of school (7)

indicatorNotes.confines of: the confines of a word are its boundary letters

annotation.surface: A school puts on an unusual workout, with secret agents joining the class.
annotation.walkthrough: PE, physical education, is the British name for school sports lessons, which suits the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Special means distinctive, set apart from the ordinary.

entries.clue: North agonises about having hardly any money (2,1,10)

annotation.surface: The North of England frets about being short of cash.
annotation.walkthrough: "North" is fodder here, spelt out in full rather than shortened to N.
annotation.definitionFit: Living on a shoestring means getting by on very little money.

entries.clue: Award touching on gallantry in part (4)

indicatorNotes.in part: the answer is part of the words

annotation.surface: A medal given partly for bravery.
annotation.walkthrough: Gong is British slang for a medal or honour.
annotation.definitionFit: A gong is informally a medal or decoration.

entries.clue: First person in main spot represented farcical situations (10)

indicatorNotes.in: ME goes inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.represented: the letters are presented again in a new order

blocks.note: me is the first person pronoun

annotation.surface: The star in the central role acted out some farces.
annotation.walkthrough: Panto is a British Christmas stage show full of slapstick; the word is used for any absurd, farcical carry-on.
annotation.definitionFit: A pantomime, figuratively, is a ridiculous or farcical situation.

entries.clue: Worker blocking sign in temporary shelter (4-2)

indicatorNotes.blocking: the worker blocks the middle of the sign

annotation.surface: A labourer stands in the way of a notice at a makeshift shelter.
annotation.walkthrough: "Sign" suggests a notice, but crosswords often mean a star sign; Leo is the lion.
annotation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shelter propped against a wall.

entries.clue: Play set point and hurry up (4,2,2)

indicatorNotes.Play: the letters are played around with

annotation.surface: A tennis player at set point is urged to get a move on.
annotation.walkthrough: "Play set point" reads as tennis; "Play" is only telling you to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Step on it, as on the accelerator, means go faster.

entries.clue: Endorsement without leading pair for trial period (9)

indicatorNotes.without leading pair: the first two letters are dropped

annotation.surface: Approval is withheld from a couple until they have served a trial run.
annotation.walkthrough: The "leading pair" is not a couple of people but the first two letters of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Probation is a period of testing someone's suitability.

entries.clue: Learner in quandary has to identify area where view is obstructed (5,4)

indicatorNotes.in: a learner caught in a quandary is inside it, so L sits inside BIND

annotation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plates British learner drivers must display.

blocks.note: being in a bind is a predicament
the L-plate of a learner driver
to spot is to pick out

annotation.surface: A learner driver in difficulty must find the part of the road they cannot see.
annotation.definitionFit: A blind spot is the area a driver cannot see.

entries.clue: Piece of wire left in taxi close to office (5)

indicatorNotes.in: L goes inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.close to: the close of office is its last letter

annotation.surface: Some wire has been left behind in a taxi near the office.
annotation.walkthrough: L sits inside CAB + E, after the whole taxi.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a cable is an insulated wire or bundle of wires carrying power or signals.

entries.clue: Second journey to get identifying outfit (5)

annotation.surface: Someone makes a second trip to pick up a uniform.
annotation.walkthrough: A strip is British for a sports team's kit, the colours that identify the side.
annotation.definitionFit: A team's strip is the outfit that marks out its players.

entries.clue: Upheaval starts to undermine real mission in work (7)

indicatorNotes.starts to: take the starting letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of undermine, real, mission

annotation.surface: Chaos threatens to derail a project at the office.
annotation.walkthrough: "Starts to" applies to all three following words, not just the first.
annotation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of great disturbance.

entries.clue: A resort given backing for sweet stuff, food in spears? (9)

indicatorNotes.given backing: the sweet stuff is written backwards

blocks.note: a spa town is a resort

annotation.surface: A holiday resort gets funding for a sweet shop and a kebab stall.
annotation.walkthrough: Asparagus is sold as spears; the question mark admits the playful definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the vegetable's edible shoots are sold and cooked as long pointed spears.

entries.clue: Tackle thing needed for a delivery? (7)

blocks.note: a verb here: to deal with a problem
what the postman must know before a parcel can arrive

annotation.surface: Someone asks what gear is required to make a delivery.
annotation.walkthrough: A delivery could also be a speech, which is another address.
annotation.definitionFit: Address means both deal with a problem and the destination on a letter.

entries.clue: Place of learning associated with staple mythical creature (7)

annotation.surface: A university is linked with a fabled beast, perhaps as its mascot.
annotation.walkthrough: "Staple" is a staple food, not the office fastener; corn is a staple crop.
annotation.definitionFit: The unicorn is a legendary horse with a single horn.

entries.clue: Earnestly try least riveting clothes (6)

indicatorNotes.clothes: the outer words clothe the answer

annotation.surface: Someone does their best to wear the dullest outfit possible.
annotation.walkthrough: "Clothes" is a verb here: the two words wrap around the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: striving is making great, earnest effort.

entries.clue: Bear, maybe, a red port in a tipsy state (8)

indicatorNotes.in a tipsy state: drunken letters stagger into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone, perhaps a bear of a man, is tipsy on a glass of red port.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bear" is a verb in the surface; as the definition it is an example of a hunting animal, flagged by "maybe".
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: bears hunt and eat other animals, so one is a kind of hunter.

entries.clue: Particular military unit (6)

blocks.note: a noun here: a single item or point
a small squad picked for a special duty

annotation.walkthrough: "Particular" reads as an adjective, but it is the noun, as in going into particulars.
annotation.definitionFit: A detail is an individual item, and also a squad assigned to a special duty.

entries.clue: Coach getting tense over damp weather (5)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, T is placed over the rest

annotation.surface: A sports coach gets nervous about the rain.
annotation.walkthrough: "Coach" could be a bus or carriage, but here it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: both mean instruct and drill someone in a skill.

entries.clue: Submission from newly constituted comic panel (10)

indicatorNotes.newly constituted: the letters are made up in a new order

annotation.surface: A newly formed panel of comedians receives an entry.
annotation.walkthrough: "Submission" suggests an entry sent to a panel, but it means yielding.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean yielding to another's will or rules.

entries.clue: Recall star, noted English runner (4)

indicatorNotes.Recall: call back, so the star comes out backwards

blocks.note: a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

annotation.surface: A famous English athlete, once a star, is remembered.
annotation.walkthrough: A runner can be a river; the Avon flows through Stratford, Shakespeare's town.
annotation.definitionFit: The Avon is a well-known English river.

entries.clue: Dull figure getting level (7)

annotation.surface: An uninteresting number evens out.
annotation.walkthrough: "Level" is the verb here.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: both mean make even, or knock down to the ground.

entries.clue: A mistake in front of elders makes one foolish (7)

indicatorNotes.front of: the front of elders is its first letter

annotation.surface: Blundering in front of your seniors makes you look silly.
annotation.walkthrough: "In front of" looks like a single phrase, but "in" is kept as printed and "front of" takes the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Asinine means stupid, from the Latin for donkey.
